Understanding Database Synchronization


Database synchronization ensures that multiple databases stay consistent with each other. This is critical for distributed systems, disaster recovery, and multi-region deployments.
Consistency issues: Keeping multiple databases in sync is complex
Latency problems: Real-time sync across regions is difficult
Data conflicts: Handling conflicting updates from multiple sources
Scaling concerns: Sync performance degrades with scale
One master database distributes changes to slave replicas.
Multiple masters replicate to each other bidirectionally.
Capture database changes and propagate them to other systems.
✅ Use transactional consistency levels

articles.author: Chem Patrick Edward
articles.description:
Hi Dev Community 👋
It’s a real pleasure to be here and an even greater privilege to learn from and share with such a brilliant community of minds. This is officially my first post, and I thought I’d start with something simple—yet meaningful.
A reminder.
If you’re reading this, I want you to know something:
You’ve got this.
Yes, times are changing. Yes, things are getting harder. But don’t let the difficulty of the present moment convince you that it defines who you are or where you’re headed. It doesn’t.
You have more to offer than you may realize, and no temporary setback has the authority to write the story of your future.
The right moment is always now.
Take ownership of today. Dust yourself off from whatever you’re carrying, and keep moving forward—valiantly. That decision to continue, even when things feel heavy, often becomes one of the most meaningful choices we ever make.
Ignore the naysayers. They don’t get a vote.
why close and honor it, because when you finally look back, let it be without regret.
Don’t allow the weight of the world to pull you into despair. Guard your mind. Protect it. Grow it. Train yourself to notice the good, even while pushing forward with the focus and resolve of someone who refuses to quit.
You can control the narrative.
So please—don’t give up.
Dust yourself off and keep going.
.
— CPE

articles.description:
I woke up at 12 p.m. today. Not ideal, not tragic. Just late.
The list below isn’t “today’s grind.”
The Four-Day Stack (Everything Done So Far)



  
  
  DSA / Leetcode


Across these four days, I worked through the following problems:
217, 242, 347, 36, 128, 217 (again), 238, 125, 167, 15, 704, 74, 153, 121, 11.
Some were clean solves.
But it’s work done regardless—and I’m counting that.
Math + ML Foundation


I went through:
Chapter 1 video
Chapter 2 video
Chapter 3 video
Chapter 4 video
All short, simple, digestible—like the 3Blue1Brown vibe but lighter.
Then:
Linear Regression
Multiple Regression
Slow foundational stuff, but it builds the base I need for later.
Today Specifically


Today was… structured in its own way.
I did my workout after a long time.
I also made a GitHub commit and marked it as Day 1 of the streak.
The Dream I Didn't Ask For


Last night, I had a dream where I was screaming into darkness.
It was one of those dreams that leaves your body tired when you wake up, like your mind fought something your muscles couldn’t see.
I’m trying to get my mental health back on track, but moments like that remind me how volatile things still are.
The Approach Changes Tomorrow


Starting tomorrow, I’m not doing four-day recaps or summaries.
that day, clean and focused.
One day at a time.
Where I Stand After Four Days



A solid chunk of DSA done
Math foundations moving steadily
Regression concepts revisited
GitHub streak restarted
Workout routine restarted
Mental state messy but functional
Still showing up
articles.title: Day 4: Four Days of Work, One Strange Dream, and a Late Start

articles.author: Somay
articles.description:
The first two days were all about laying foundations: 2 videos on vectors from 3Blue1Brown, and tackling Leetcode problems 217, 242, 1, 347, 128, 74, 704, and 153. Honestly? I didn’t approach them with full integrity. I tried, got stuck, and ended up looking at hints or solutions. My plan is to revisit each of these problems later with zero shortcuts—this is my metric for real progress. Linear and multiple regression also got some attention, but that’s just the technical side.
Beyond work, last night reminded me how fragile control can feel. I hit a near-breaking point but somehow held it together. I’m attempting a new perspective on life: not to succeed flawlessly, but to keep moving, keep observing, and keep recalibrating even if I stumble. The real experiment starts tomorrow, both with code and with myself.
articles.title: Day 3: Reflecting and pushing.

articles.author: Somay
articles.description:
Day 2 wasn’t impressive. I woke up feeling slow, and being at my grandma’s house doesn’t help. It’s one of those environments where everyone cares a little too loudly, and it kills any sense of pace. Not in a toxic way, just not compatible with how I function.
Still, I worked.
I watched the 3Blue1Brown video on vectors, which cleared things up more than any textbook explanation has. After that, I moved into hashing and stacks. Hashing still feels rough—it doesn’t click as naturally as other topics. No point pretending otherwise.
I solved LeetCode 217, 242, and 1. Then I had to take a nap because someone managed to irritate me enough to shut my brain down for an hour. After that, I went through linear regression.
That’s the whole list for today. Nothing dramatic. Nothing aesthetic. Just work done in a slow, unfriendly headspace.
I’m not tired, but I do feel a bit dead inside—more like I’m back in the same isolation I always return to. It’s not new, not scary, just familiar. Day 2 is over. Day 3 will be cleaner.
articles.title: Day 2: Low Energy, Work Done Anyway

articles.author: Somay
articles.description:
Starting from a clean slate feels strange, but necessary. After wiping everything and restarting the account, today became the first day of the new cycle. No legacy posts, no old signals bleeding into what I’m building now.
I started simple: posted the comeback, then sat down and built out my ML and DSA roadmaps for the month. Nothing fancy—just a clear structure of what needs to happen daily and what’s non-negotiable. I’m keeping both roadmaps practical and heavy on consistency rather than pushing unrealistic volume.
If anyone wants those roadmaps, reach out. You can mail me at somaykaush@gmail.com. I’m keeping them open because someone else might benefit from a clean, no-nonsense path.
There’s another piece to this: I’m not planning to rot in front of a laptop all month. Workouts start again on Monday. Coding + training—not for aesthetics, not for internet points, but because the mix keeps me stable. If you’re following along, you’ll have to handle both. It’s part of the rhythm I’m setting for this reset.
Day 1 wasn’t dramatic. It wasn’t loud. But it was a proper start.
The rest builds from here.
articles.title: Day 1: Found the map
